predecessors.name: Nanda Empire
predecessors.text: Kalinga, 'believed to be briefly annexed by Nanda ruler Mahapadma Nanda between 345 and 340 BCE'; 'Kalingas broke away from the empire of Magadha in 322 BCE'

successors.name: Mahameghavahana dynasty
successors.text: Kalinga under the Mahameghavahana family: 'After the Mauryan decline, the region came under the Mahameghavahana family'; infobox regnal dates give the founder as 170 BCE

ledger.x: 322 BCE: Kalinga breaks away from Magadha as Chandragupta Maurya rebels against the Nandas.
262 BCE: Ashoka's war on Kalinga begins.
261 BCE: the war ends in Kalinga's defeat.
261 BCE: Kalinga is annexed by the Mauryan Empire.
224 BCE: Kalinga regains its independence from the Mauryas.
171 BCE: Kalinga passes to the Mahameghavahana family.

wars.name: Kalinga War
wars.outcome: Mauryan victory: Kalinga annexed, about 100,000 killed and 150,000 deported by Ashoka's own figures; Ashoka afterwards ends military expansion.

certainty.note: The page defines Kalinga by rivers (between the Ganges and the Godavari, northern limit disputed between the Mahanadi, Baitarani and Ganges) and by Odisha's modern extent; no treaty or survey line exists.
